quick_questions.unconscious: A person is unconscious but breathing. What should I do?
quick_questions.bleeding: Severe arm bleeding will not stop. What are the steps?
quick_questions.burn: A hot water burn. What should I do now?

bleeding.title: Severe bleeding
bleeding.summary: Stop bleeding with direct pressure and watch for shock until help arrives.

0.title: Secure the area first
0.description: Approach only if the scene is safe. Call emergency services now — severe bleeding requires immediate help.

1.title: Apply direct pressure
1.description: Place clean gauze or cloth over the wound and press firmly without checking repeatedly.

2.title: Add layers without removing the first
2.description: If blood soaks through, add another clean layer and keep pressure.

3.title: Do not remove embedded objects
3.description: Press around the object and stabilize it until help arrives.

4.title: Watch for shock
4.description: Keep the person lying down if possible, warm them, and seek urgent help for paleness, cold sweat, dizziness, or confusion.

unconscious.title: Unconscious but breathing
unconscious.summary: Check breathing, protect the airway, and do not give anything by mouth.

0.title: Check response
0.description: Call the person clearly and tap their shoulder gently. Do not shake them hard.

1.title: Check breathing quickly
1.description: Look, listen, and feel for breathing for no more than 10 seconds.

2.title: Keep the airway open
2.description: If breathing is present, monitor continuously and avoid moving the neck or back if injury is possible.

3.title: Use recovery position when safe
3.description: If no neck or back injury is suspected, place them on their side to help keep the airway open.

4.title: Give nothing by mouth
4.description: Do not give water, food, or medicine. Call emergency services immediately and stay with them until help arrives.

fracture.title: Fractures and bone injuries
fracture.summary: Immobilize the injury, reduce movement, and monitor feeling and circulation.

0.title: Do not move the injury
0.description: Ask the person not to move the injured limb or area.

1.title: Support gently
1.description: Stabilize the area in a comfortable position using cloth, padding, or a temporary splint if available.

2.title: Cover open wounds
2.description: Cover bleeding or exposed bone with a clean dressing without pressing on exposed bone.

3.title: Use a cold pack
3.description: If the skin is unbroken, apply a wrapped cold pack near (not on) the injury to reduce pain and swelling. Never place ice on bare skin or near open wounds.

4.title: Watch danger signs
4.description: Call emergency services for severe pain, deformity, numbness, bluish color, cold fingers, open bleeding, or any head, neck, or back injury — do not move the person.

burns.title: Burns
burns.summary: Cool the burn with running water, protect it from contamination, and avoid home remedies.

0.title: Stop the burning source
0.description: Move the person away from heat, electricity, steam, or chemicals only when safe.

1.title: Cool for 20 minutes
1.description: Cool the burn under cool to lukewarm running water for about 20 minutes. Do not use cold or iced water.

2.title: Remove tight items
2.description: Remove rings, watches, or loose clothing before swelling begins. Do not remove anything stuck to skin.

3.title: Cover gently
3.description: Cover with a sterile non-stick dressing or clean cloth. Do not apply oils, toothpaste, butter, random creams, or herbs.

4.title: Call emergency immediately for serious burns
4.description: Call emergency services immediately for electrical, chemical, large, deep, facial, or burns to hands, feet, or sensitive areas — do not wait to finish first aid before calling.

cpr.title: CPR
cpr.summary: Start chest compressions when the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.

0.title: Check response and breathing
0.description: Call and tap gently. If there is no response and no normal breathing, treat it as an emergency.

1.title: Call emergency services and get AED
1.description: Ask a specific person to call emergency services and bring an AED if available. If an AED arrives, turn it on immediately and follow its voice instructions.

2.title: Start chest compressions
2.description: Place the heel of your hand in the center of the chest. Push down firmly at least 5 cm (2 inches) at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute.

3.title: Allow chest recoil
3.description: Let the chest return fully after each compression and minimize pauses.

4.title: Continue until help arrives
4.description: Continue until normal breathing returns, responders arrive, an AED takes over, or you cannot continue.

choking.title: Choking
choking.summary: Act quickly when the person cannot speak or breathe because the airway is blocked.

0.title: Assess coughing ability
0.description: If the person can cough strongly or speak, encourage coughing and monitor.

1.title: Start back blows
1.description: If they cannot speak or breathe, lean them forward and give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.

2.title: Move to abdominal thrusts
2.description: If the object does not come out, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts inward and upward for adults and children over one year. For pregnant persons, use chest thrusts instead (push inward on the center of the chest).

3.title: Repeat and call for help
3.description: Alternate 5 back blows and 5 thrusts until breathing improves or help arrives.

4.title: If unconscious
4.description: Lower them carefully to a firm surface. Start chest compressions immediately — push hard and fast in the center of the chest. Do not sweep the mouth unless you can clearly see and remove the object.
